new_task_1.title: Preserve supported pandas extension arrays during DataFrame roundtrips
new_task_1.description: xarray now preserves supported one-dimensional pandas extension arrays when ingesting pandas Series or DataFrame objects and when roundtripping through Dataset.from_dataframe() and to_pandas(). Instead of converting every pandas object to .values, xarray keeps extension-array-backed data in its PandasExtensionArray wrapper for compatible dtypes such as categorical, interval, and pyarrow-backed nullable integer arrays. At the same time, explicitly unsupported extension arrays, including DatetimeArray, TimedeltaArray, and NumPy-backed NumpyExtensionArray subclasses, are coerced to NumPy arrays so they continue to work without relying on unsupported duck-array behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray correctly handles pandas extension arrays when converting from pandas objects into Variables and Datasets. Compatible extension arrays should retain their extension-array semantics through xarray storage and back to pandas, while unsupported extension-array implementations must be converted to plain NumPy arrays to avoid incorrect wrapping or indexing behavior.

expectation.grounded: When xarray receives a pandas Series or DataFrame column with an extension-array dtype, it must preserve the underlying ExtensionArray instead of blindly taking .values, unless the array is one of the explicitly unsupported classes: pandas DatetimeArray, TimedeltaArray, or NumpyExtensionArray subclasses. Compatible extension arrays must be wrapped with xarray's PandasExtensionArray support so Dataset.from_dataframe(...)[name].to_pandas() roundtrips values and dtype correctly for both columns and indexes. Unsupported extension arrays must be converted with to_numpy()/np.asarray so xarray stores them as NumPy data rather than as extension-array wrappers.
expectation.conceptual: xarray should roundtrip supported pandas extension arrays faithfully and selectively. Users should see extension dtypes preserved where xarray can actually support them, and should see a stable NumPy fallback for extension-array types that are not safe to expose through xarray's duck-array path.

constraints.grounded: The change must not alter the values produced by Dataset.from_dataframe() or DataArray.to_pandas(). Internal wrapping logic must reject NumPy-backed NumpyExtensionArray objects from the PandasExtensionArray adapter. Any internal operations that inspect dimensionality for these wrapped arrays must use a duck-array-compatible ndim path so lazy indexing and scalar wrapping continue to work.
constraints.conceptual: The feature should improve pandas interoperability without broadening support to extension-array types that xarray still cannot handle safely. Unsupported dtypes should degrade predictably to NumPy arrays rather than failing or producing partially wrapped objects.

behavior: Supported one-dimensional pandas extension arrays are preserved when ingesting pandas Series or DataFrame columns into xarray variables
Dataset.from_dataframe(...)[name].to_pandas() preserves both values and extension dtype for compatible extension arrays such as categorical, interval, and pyarrow-backed nullable integer arrays
The same roundtrip behavior applies when the extension array is used as the pandas index instead of a column
DatetimeArray, TimedeltaArray, and NumPy-backed NumpyExtensionArray subclasses are treated as unsupported and converted to plain NumPy arrays inside xarray
Lazy indexing and duck-array access for supported PandasExtensionArray-backed data continue to function correctly because dimensionality checks use a duck-array-compatible ndim path
acceptance_criteria: Given a pandas DataFrame with a categorical, interval, or compatible pyarrow-backed extension array column, when converting with Dataset.from_dataframe(df)[name] and then calling to_pandas(), then the returned pandas object has the same values and the same extension dtype as the original column

Given a pandas DataFrame whose index is a supported extension array, when converting through xarray and back to pandas, then the returned pandas object preserves the original index values and extension dtype
Given a pandas Series or DataFrame column backed by DatetimeArray or TimedeltaArray, when ingesting it into xarray, then xarray stores it as NumPy data rather than a PandasExtensionArray wrapper

Given a pandas StringArray or other NumpyExtensionArray-backed dtype, when roundtripping through xarray, then values are preserved but xarray falls back to NumPy storage instead of preserving the extension dtype
Given lazily indexed xarray data backed by a supported PandasExtensionArray, when performing duck-array access or vectorized indexing, then the operation succeeds and returns the expected values
